## Summary

Eisman sees defensive rotation beneath a flat index and expects private-credit liquidity restrictions to spread. He favors payment networks, Moody's proprietary franchises, Quanta infrastructure and Meritage value, while preferring Netflix without Warner Bros. His Nvidia operating outlook was supported. Conditional recession positioning is selective because AI-sensitive utilities and troubled health insurers may not behave defensively. He uses charts as a trigger to revisit fundamentals, while explicitly declining to forecast an imminent recession.

Full transcript read. This bounded evidence audit retains unresolved outcomes where matched primary verification is missing; those are not adverse accuracy grades.

## Framework and tools

- Separate index performance from sector rotation.
- Analyze redemption rights against asset liquidity.
- Favor proprietary databases, duopolies and physical infrastructure.
- Choose defensive businesses at the subsector level rather than rely on labels.
- Use charts to revisit fundamentals and avoid newly collapsing stocks.

Tools and charts discussed, not a complete visual inspection:

- Technology/software/staples relative returns
- Private fund redemption policy
- Homebuilder price/tangible book
- Nvidia capex demand
- Moody's proprietary data
- Carvana short interest and days to cover
- Walmart forward P/E
- Recession sector classification
- Chart basing

## Source cautions

Steve Eisman is the sole substantive speaker; viewer questions are distinguished from his responses.
- Recorded February 19, published February 20.
- Teaser is repeated material.
- Caption says Edison International/EIX then ConEd later; preserve the two named examples rather than silently treating them as the same utility.
- The statement that no recession occurred since the GFC does not explicitly exclude the pandemic.
